The CVE-2026-34155 fix in RAUC 1.15.2 refuses a plain-format payload larger than INT32_MAX (2 GiB) both when signing and when verifying, with the error 'Bundle payload size … exceeds maximum for bundles using plain format (2 GiB)'
With bundle-formats restricted, RAUC refuses a disallowed format with 'Bundle format 'plain' not allowed' (check_allowed_bundle_format)

Debian rauc versions on 2026-11-11: stable (trixie) 1.13-3+deb13u1, testing and unstable 1.15.2-1, oldstable 1.8-2, no backports package; apt in a Debian 13.7 VM with trixie-backports enabled offers only 1.13-3+deb13u1

Lab T12 (arm64, one 2.1 GiB random payload): upstream RAUC 1.15.2 and Debian rauc 1.13-3+deb13u1 both refuse to create a plain bundle ('exceeds maximum for bundles using plain format (2 GiB)'); 1.15.2 creates the verity bundle (2,272,204,851 bytes); unfixed upstream v1.15.1 creates the plain bundle (2,254,444,227 bytes), and both fixed builds refuse to verify that bundle with the same error. No bundle was installed

For a plain bundle RAUC 1.15.2 identifies the format by its detached signature and runs the full CMS verification over the payload (cms_verify_fd) before the bundle-formats check, so a verity-only device still refuses a plain bundle but only after hashing the whole payload (22-66 s for a 1.7 GB image under TCG in this lab)

In RAUC 1.15.2 'rauc install' with the D-Bus service enabled has no --override-boot-slot/--keyring options (they exist only when built with service=false), and r_mark_active calls only the bootloader's set-primary for the target slot (no set-state good during install)

Raspberry Pi firmware tryboot is a one-shot flag cleared before the firmware starts, so 'a crash or reset will cause the original config.txt file to be loaded on the next reboot'; it is set with reboot '0 tryboot'; with secure-boot enabled tryboot loads tryboot.img instead of boot.img; tryboot_a_b is implicitly 1 inside a boot.img ramdisk

Raspberry Pi documents partition-level A/B with autoboot.txt in the first FAT partition ([all] tryboot_a_b=1 boot_partition=2, [tryboot] boot_partition=3), separate boot FAT partitions 2/3 and root partitions 4/5, a [boot_partition=N] filter to pick cmdline per slot, commit by swapping autoboot.txt, and the booted partition and tryboot flag readable from /proc/device-tree/chosen/bootloader/ as 32-bit big-endian integers

Home Assistant OS's Pi 5 RAUC backend arms tryboot via /run/systemd/reboot-param ('0 tryboot'), commits by rewriting config.txt/cmdline.txt when /proc/device-tree/chosen/bootloader/tryboot is set, and on a later normal boot drops a staged tryboot that missed its one attempt and marks that slot bad (drop_stale_tryboot); slots are os_prefix folders slot-A/ slot-B/ in one boot partition
The Raspberry Pi boot_count variable is an 8-bit value in a reset-safe register, incremented at boot and cleared if power is disconnected; readable at /proc/device-tree/chosen/bootloader/count

Raspberry Pi Imager's OS list on 2026-11-11 offers 'Raspberry Pi OS Lite (64-bit)' release 2026-10-06 (trixie) for pi5-64bit; the .img.xz sha256 483db18a…2843 matches the published .sha256 and the extracted image sha256 b8a393dc…8780 matches extract_sha256

Desk pre-flight (arm64 VM, loop device as target, real Raspberry Pi OS Lite 2026-10-06 tree): prepare-disk.sh built the 7-partition MBR layout with 7 verity + 1 plain bundles; under the device's own system.conf RAUC 1.15.2 accepted good, refused plain-good ('Bundle format 'plain' not allowed') and wrong-key; a real install wrote boot B + root B, wrote the trial marker 'B 2', armed '0 tryboot' and left autoboot.txt unchanged; the backend committed B only with a faked tryboot boot from partition 3 and refused a commit without tryboot. Found and fixed: the backend reported 'armed' when /run/systemd was missing [firmware, watchdog, panics and power loss not testable here]

RAUC v1.15.2 builds from the pinned upstream commit with Debian 13 (trixie) libraries only, natively for arm64 and in an amd64 buildd chroot under qemu-user (meson, -Dtests=false), and replaces Debian's rauc/rauc-service packages in a Debian 13 amd64 image with unchanged gate scripts; its runtime libraries come from Debian (libglib2.0-0t64, libssl3t64, libcurl4t64, libjson-glib-1.0-0, libfdisk1, libnl-genl-3-200)

Lab (Debian 13 x86_64 in QEMU TCG, 2 sequential runs, same build): with upstream RAUC 1.15.2 and bundle-formats=verity the k3s fresh-signal gate suite of LAB-rauc-k3s-gate repeated: good update committed after 3 fresh passes (87-148 s), bad-k3s and stale-Ready (bad-noagent) rolled back at the 300 s deadline, kernel panic and watchdog hang each tried 3 times then fell back and were never retried, power cut mid-write and in the commit window recovered without input; a validly signed plain bundle was refused ('Bundle format 'plain' not allowed') with no trial marker; the naive gate committed a kubelet-less system in both runs [run 2 all PASS; run 1 all PASS except T11 driver bug]
